topic.title: Sine and Cosine Function Values
topic.summary: The coordinates (r cos θ, r sin θ) of a point on a circle centered at the origin, and exact sine and cosine values for multiples of π/4 and π/6 from special right triangles.

variants.stem: A circle with radius 12 is centered at the origin. The terminal ray of an angle θ = 5π/6 in standard position meets the circle at the point P.

parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of P.
Find the y-coordinate of P.
The terminal ray of θ + π meets the same circle at the point Q. Write the coordinates of Q.

solution: For a circle of radius r, x = r cos θ. So x = 12 cos(5π/6) = 12(−√3/2) = −6√3.
Adding π turns the ray half a revolution, so Q is the point on the opposite side of the origin: (6√3, −6).

variants.stem: Give exact values, with no calculator.

parts.prompt: Find sin(19π/6).
Find cos(4π/3).
Where does the terminal ray of 240° meet the unit circle? Write the point as (x, y).

solution: The terminal ray of 19π/6, which is also the terminal ray of 7π/6, makes a π/6 angle with the x-axis and is in Quadrant III. So sin(19π/6) = −1/2.
The terminal ray of 4π/3 makes a π/3 angle with the x-axis and is in Quadrant III. So cos(4π/3) = −1/2.
240° = 4π/3 radians. The point is (cos 4π/3, sin 4π/3) = (−1/2, −√3/2).

variants.stem: A Ferris wheel has radius 16 meters, and its center is 26 meters above the ground. A seat on the rim starts level with the center, on the right side. The Ferris wheel turns counterclockwise through an angle θ.

parts.prompt: How high above the ground is the seat when θ = 5π/6?
When θ = 5π/3, how far is the seat to the right of the center? Use a negative number if it is to the left.
How high above the ground is the seat when θ = π/2?

solution: The height is 26 + 16 sin θ. At θ = 5π/6, sin θ = 1/2, so the height is 26 + 16(1/2) = 34 meters.
The horizontal distance from the center is 16 cos θ. At θ = 5π/3, cos θ = 1/2, so it is 16(1/2) = 8 meters.
At θ = π/2, sin θ = 1, so the height is 26 + 16(1) = 42 meters.

variants.stem: An angle θ = 11π/6 is in standard position.

parts.prompt: Find the reference angle, the acute angle between the terminal ray and the x-axis.
Is cos θ positive or negative?
Find sin θ.

solution: The terminal ray is in Quadrant IV, and the angle between it and the x-axis is π/6.
In Quadrant IV, the x-coordinate on the circle is positive, so cos θ is positive.
The value of sin at the reference angle π/6 is 1/2. In Quadrant IV the sign is negative, so sin θ = −1/2.

variants.stem: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position, with 0 ≤ θ < 2π, meets a circle centered at the origin at the point (8√3, 8).

parts.prompt: Find the radius of the circle.
Find cos θ.
Find θ.

solution: The distance from the origin to the point is the radius: r = √((8√3)² + 8²) = √256 = 16.
Since x = r cos θ, cos θ = x/r = (8√3)/16 = √3/2.
Likewise sin θ = y/r = 1/2. The point is in Quadrant I, with reference angle π/6, so θ = π/6.

The height is 42 + 40 sin θ = 42 + 40(1/2) = 62 centimeters.
The horizontal distance from the axle is 40 cos θ = 40(−√3/2) = −20√3 centimeters.

variants.stem: A windmill has radius 40 meters, and its hub is 43 meters above the ground. The tip of a blade starts level with the hub, on the right side. The windmill turns counterclockwise and makes one full revolution every 8 minutes.

parts.prompt: Through what angle θ, in radians, has the windmill turned after 7 minutes?
How high above the ground is the tip of the blade at that time?
At that time, how far is the tip of the blade to the right of the hub? Use a negative number if it is to the left.

solution: One revolution is 2π radians and takes 8 minutes, so after 7 minutes the angle is 2π(7/8) = 7π/4.
The height is 43 + 40 sin θ = 43 + 40(−√2/2) = 43 − 20√2 meters.
The horizontal distance from the hub is 40 cos θ = 40(√2/2) = 20√2 meters.
